1925-10-01.head: Chilean President Alessandri Resigns
1925-10-01.body: President Arturo Alessandri of Chile has resigned office. Vice-President Luis Barros Borgoño has taken over as acting president.

1925-10-02.head: Spanish Troops Enter Rif Capital Ajdir
1925-10-02.body: Spanish forces have entered Ajdir, the capital of Abd el-Krim's Rif Republic in Morocco, in the combined Franco-Spanish offensive.

1925-10-02.head: Fascist Unions and Employers Sign Rome Pact
1925-10-02.body: The Pact of the Vidoni Palace was signed in Rome between Fascist labour syndicates and the industrialists' confederation, giving the Fascist unions sole right to represent workers.

1925-10-02.head: Scots Inventor Transmits Image by Wireless
1925-10-02.body: Mr John Logie Baird, working in Frith Street, London, has transmitted a recognisable picture of a ventriloquist's dummy by his television apparatus, and afterwards the face of an office boy.

1925-10-03.head: American Aircraft Carrier Lexington Launched
1925-10-03.body: The United States Navy's aircraft carrier Lexington, converted from a battle cruiser hull under the Washington Treaty, was launched at Quincy, Massachusetts.

1925-10-04.head: Rising Against French at Hama
1925-10-04.body: Rebels led by Fawzi al-Qawuqji have attacked French mandate posts in the Syrian city of Hama. Heavy fighting has been reported.

1925-10-04.head: Finnish Torpedo Boat Lost With All Hands
1925-10-04.body: The Finnish Navy torpedo boat S2 has foundered in a fierce storm off Pori in the Gulf of Bothnia. All 53 of her crew are lost.

1925-10-05.head: Security Conference Opens at Locarno
1925-10-05.body: Delegates of Britain, France, Germany, Italy, Belgium, Poland and Czechoslovakia met at Locarno, Switzerland, to negotiate a security pact and Germany's entry into the League of Nations.

1925-10-05.head: Pan-American Highway Conference Opens
1925-10-05.body: The first conference of American republics to discuss a highway linking the continent opened at Buenos Aires.

1925-10-06.head: Locarno Debates French Guarantees to Poland
1925-10-06.body: The Locarno Conference debated France's demand for the right to cross German territory to aid Poland and Czechoslovakia in the event of war.
1925-10-06.note: Locarno debate reported during the first days of the conference; the month page's day heading could not be read cleanly.

1925-10-07.head: Locarno Deadlock Over Eastern Frontiers
1925-10-07.body: German and French delegates at Locarno have reached a deadlock over the question of guarantees for Poland and Czechoslovakia.
1925-10-07.note: Ongoing Locarno story; the day heading on the month page could not be read cleanly.

1925-10-07.head: Christy Mathewson Dies
1925-10-07.body: Christy Mathewson, 45, the famous American baseball pitcher, has died of tuberculosis at Saranac Lake, New York.

1925-10-08.head: Mona Lisa Thief Peruggia Dies
1925-10-08.body: Vincenzo Peruggia, the Italian who stole the Mona Lisa from the Louvre in 1911, has died of heart failure in France on his 44th birthday.

1925-10-09.head: Hugo Preuss, Author of Weimar Constitution, Dies
1925-10-09.body: Dr Hugo Preuss, 64, the jurist who drafted the German Republic's constitution of 1919, has died in Berlin.

1925-10-09.head: Serbian Pretender Obrenović Dies in Poverty
1925-10-09.body: George Obrenović, 35, son of King Milan of Serbia and claimant to the Serbian throne, has died in poverty in Hungary.

1925-10-10.head: Forbidden City Opened as Palace Museum
1925-10-10.body: The former Qing imperial palace at Peking was opened to the public as the Palace Museum on the Chinese national day, housing over a million works of art.

1925-10-10.head: Italian Train Plunges From Flooded Bridge
1925-10-10.body: About 15 persons were killed near Catanzaro, Italy, when a train fell from a bridge weakened by flood waters.

1925-10-10.head: Tobacco Magnate James B. Duke Dies
1925-10-10.body: James Buchanan Duke, 68, founder of the American Tobacco Company and benefactor of Duke University, has died of pneumonia in New York.

1925-10-11.head: Locarno Powers Settle League Obligations Question
1925-10-11.body: Powers at Locarno agreed that Germany's special military position would be considered in her League obligations until general disarmament, removing the chief obstacle to German entry into the League.
1925-10-11.note: Page lists this beside the fourth World Series game (11 October); dated accordingly.

1925-10-11.head: Federal Agent Shot Dead in Chicago
1925-10-11.body: Edwin C. Shanahan, an agent of the United States Bureau of Investigation, was shot dead in Chicago while arresting car thief Martin Durkin.

1925-10-12.head: Paris Riots Against Rif War
1925-10-12.body: Two persons were killed and 70 arrested in Paris during Communist demonstrations against French involvement in the Rif War. Deputy Jacques Doriot was among those detained.

1925-10-12.head: Germany and Soviet Union Sign Trade Treaty
1925-10-12.body: Germany and the Soviet Union have signed a commercial treaty intended to increase trade between the two countries.

1925-10-12.head: American Troops Land in Panama
1925-10-12.body: Some 600 United States soldiers have entered Panama City at the request of President Chiari to put down disorders arising from a tenants' strike.

1925-10-13.head: British Seamen's Strike Ends
1925-10-13.body: The unofficial strike of British seamen has come to an end at home ports, though the stoppage continues in Australia.

1925-10-13.head: U.S. War Secretary Weeks Resigns
1925-10-13.body: John W. Weeks has resigned as United States Secretary of War owing to failing health.

1925-10-14.head: Rioting in Damascus Over Displayed Corpses
1925-10-14.body: Rioting broke out in Damascus after French troops publicly displayed the bodies of Druze rebels. French forces withdrew from parts of the city.

1925-10-14.head: Strongman Eugen Sandow Dies
1925-10-14.body: Eugen Sandow, 58, the famous strongman and physical culture teacher, has died in London.

1925-10-14.head: Entomologist Killed Testing Poison Gas
1925-10-14.body: Professor Harold Maxwell-Lefroy, 48, of the Imperial College, London, has died after an accident in his laboratory while experimenting with gases to destroy houseflies.

1925-10-15.head: Pittsburgh Wins American Baseball Series
1925-10-15.body: The Pittsburgh Pirates defeated the Washington Senators 9 to 7 in the seventh and deciding game of baseball's World Series.

1925-10-15.head: New Stadium Opened in Seoul
1925-10-15.body: The Keijo (Seoul) Stadium, later to be known as Dongdaemun Stadium, has been opened in the Korean capital.

1925-10-16.head: Locarno Pacts Initialled; 'New Era' Hailed
1925-10-16.body: The Locarno Conference closed with its treaties initialled. Herr Stresemann spoke of a new era in European relations, and M. Briand of an epoch of co-operation and friendship.

1925-10-17.head: Twelve Killed in Italian Rail Collision
1925-10-17.body: Twelve persons were killed and twenty injured in a railway collision on the Milan-Genoa line.

1925-10-18.head: Syrian Rebels Enter Damascus
1925-10-18.body: Druze and nationalist insurgents have entered Damascus, setting fires and seizing the Azm Palace. Heavy French losses are reported.

1925-10-18.head: Turkey and Bulgaria Sign Friendship Treaty
1925-10-18.body: Turkey and Bulgaria have signed a treaty of friendship dealing with the rights of the Turkish minority in Bulgaria.

1925-10-19.head: French Guns Bombard Damascus
1925-10-19.body: French artillery and aircraft have bombarded the Hariqa quarter of Damascus, where rebels had taken refuge. Much of the quarter is reported destroyed.

1925-10-19.head: Greek-Bulgarian Border Clash at Petrich
1925-10-19.body: A Greek soldier has been killed in an incident on the Bulgarian frontier near Petrich, reportedly after crossing the line in pursuit of his dog. Firing has followed.

1925-10-20.head: Coolidge Orders Court-Martial of Colonel Mitchell
1925-10-20.body: President Coolidge has directed that Colonel William Mitchell be tried by court-martial for insubordination over his public criticism of the Army and Navy air services.

1925-10-21.head: Greece Sends Ultimatum to Bulgaria
1925-10-21.body: Greece has delivered a 48-hour ultimatum to Bulgaria demanding an apology and indemnity for the Petrich frontier incident.

1925-10-22.head: Greek Army Crosses Into Bulgaria
1925-10-22.body: Greek troops have invaded Bulgarian territory near Petrich to enforce their government's demands for satisfaction.

1925-10-22.head: Physicist Files Patent on Electric Current Control
1925-10-22.body: Dr Julius Lilienfeld has filed a patent application in Canada for a device to control electric currents in solid materials, proposed as a substitute for the wireless valve.

1925-10-23.head: Briand Summons League Over Balkan Invasion
1925-10-23.body: M. Briand, as President of the League Council, has called an extraordinary session of the League of Nations to deal with the Greek-Bulgarian conflict.

1925-10-24.head: Chile Votes Directly for President
1925-10-24.body: Chile has held its first direct presidential election. Emiliano Figueroa won with over 70 per cent of the vote.

1925-10-24.head: National Boys' Clubs Association Formed
1925-10-24.body: A National Association of Boys' Clubs has been founded in Britain to bring together youth organisations.

1925-10-25.head: Melkite Patriarch Demetrius Qadi Dies
1925-10-25.body: Demetrius I Qadi, 64, Patriarch of the Melkite Greek Catholic Church, has died.

1925-10-25.head: Swiss Elections Held
1925-10-25.body: Switzerland has held elections to the National Council. The Free Democratic Party has retained its position as the largest party.

1925-10-25.head: Chamorro Seizes Managua Fortress
1925-10-25.body: Former Nicaraguan President Emiliano Chamorro has seized La Loma fortress overlooking Managua and demanded the post of Minister of War.

1925-10-26.head: League Orders Greece and Bulgaria to Cease Fire
1925-10-26.body: The League Council, meeting in Paris, has ordered Greece and Bulgaria to stop hostilities within 24 hours and withdraw their troops behind the frontier.

1925-10-26.head: American Wins Schneider Trophy at Record Speed
1925-10-26.body: Lieutenant James Doolittle of the U.S. Army has won the Schneider Trophy seaplane race at Baltimore at a record speed of 232.57 miles per hour.

1925-10-26.head: Chamorro Made Nicaraguan War Minister
1925-10-26.body: President Solórzano of Nicaragua has appointed General Emiliano Chamorro Minister of War, effectively yielding control of the army.

1925-10-27.head: Water Skis Patented in America
1925-10-27.body: Mr Fred Waller of New York has been granted a patent for water skis, to be sold as 'Dolphin Akwa-Skees'.
1925-10-27.note: Minor item; the page lists it among events of 26–27 October.

1925-10-28.head: Tutankhamun's Golden Mask Revealed
1925-10-28.body: Mr Howard Carter has opened the innermost coffin of Tutankhamun at Luxor, revealing the King's mummy covered by a mask of gold and lapis lazuli.

1925-10-28.head: Mitchell Court-Martial Opens in Washington
1925-10-28.body: The court-martial of Colonel William Mitchell on charges of insubordination has opened in Washington.

1925-10-29.head: Canadian Election: Conservatives Gain
1925-10-29.body: In the Canadian general election the Conservatives increased their seats from 49 to 115, while Mr Mackenzie King's Liberals fell to 100.

1925-10-29.head: Greece Completes Withdrawal From Bulgaria
1925-10-29.body: Greek troops have completed their withdrawal from Bulgarian territory. The League of Nations is to appoint a commission to fix responsibility and assess damages.

1925-10-30.head: Lehár's 'Paganini' Premiered in Vienna
1925-10-30.body: Franz Lehár's new operetta 'Paganini' had its first performance at the Johann Strauss Theatre in Vienna.

1925-10-30.head: Angkor Ruins Placed Under Protection
1925-10-30.body: The Governor-General of French Indochina has issued a decree protecting the ruins of Angkor in Cambodia.

1925-10-31.head: Persian Parliament Deposes Qajar Dynasty
1925-10-31.body: The Persian Majlis has deposed the absent Ahmad Shah and ended the Qajar dynasty, entrusting provisional government to the Prime Minister, Reza Khan.

1925-10-31.head: Soviet War Commissar Frunze Dies
1925-10-31.body: Mikhail Frunze, 40, People's Commissar for Military and Naval Affairs of the Soviet Union, has died following a surgical operation in Moscow.

1925-10-31.head: British Empire Exhibition Closes at Wembley
1925-10-31.body: The British Empire Exhibition closed at Wembley. The Duke of York addressed a crowd of some 40,000 at the Empire Stadium.

1925-11-01.head: Sikh Gurdwaras Act Takes Effect
1925-11-01.body: The Sikh Gurdwaras Act has come into force in the Punjab, placing Sikh shrines under the control of an elected Sikh body.

1925-11-01.head: Seventeen Killed in Ruhr Mine Blast
1925-11-01.body: An explosion in a mine near Gelsenkirchen, Germany, has killed 17 miners.

1925-11-02.head: Welsh Dam Bursts; Sixteen Dead
1925-11-02.body: A dam above Dolgarrog in North Wales burst after heavy rain, sending a flood through the village. Sixteen persons have been killed.

1925-11-02.head: Poland Buries Unknown Soldier in Warsaw
1925-11-02.body: An unknown Polish soldier has been interred at the Tomb of the Unknown Soldier in Warsaw.

1925-11-02.head: New Victor Phonograph Plays Electrical Records
1925-11-02.body: The Victor Talking Machine Company has placed on sale its Orthophonic Victrola, designed to play the new electrically recorded gramophone records.

1925-11-03.head: Jimmy Walker Elected Mayor of New York
1925-11-03.body: Mr James J. Walker, Democrat, has been elected Mayor of New York City.

1925-11-04.head: Plot to Kill Mussolini Foiled
1925-11-04.body: Italian police have arrested the Socialist deputy Tito Zaniboni in a Rome hotel room, where a rifle was found trained on the balcony from which Signor Mussolini was to speak.

1925-11-04.head: Coates Wins New Zealand Election
1925-11-04.body: The Reform Party under Mr Gordon Coates has won 56 of the 80 seats in the New Zealand general election.

1925-11-05.head: Physiologist J. N. Langley Dies
1925-11-05.body: Professor John Newport Langley, 73, the Cambridge physiologist known for his work on the nervous system, has died.

1925-11-05.head: War Film 'The Big Parade' Opens
1925-11-05.body: The war picture 'The Big Parade' had its premiere at Grauman's Egyptian Theatre in Hollywood.

1925-11-06.head: Emperor Khai Dinh of Annam Dies
1925-11-06.body: Emperor Khai Dinh of Annam has died at Hué. His young son, now at school in France, succeeds him.

1925-11-06.head: Voroshilov Named Soviet War Commissar
1925-11-06.body: Kliment Voroshilov has been appointed People's Commissar for Military and Naval Affairs in succession to the late Mikhail Frunze.

1925-11-07.head: Italian Opposition Leaders Arrested
1925-11-07.body: Several Italian opposition leaders have been arrested in connection with the plot against Signor Mussolini.

1925-11-07.head: France to Return Richthofen's Remains
1925-11-07.body: France has agreed to the return to Germany of the remains of the airman Manfred von Richthofen.

1925-11-08.head: Portugal Holds General Election
1925-11-08.body: Portugal has held parliamentary elections, in which the Democratic Party gained a majority of 83 seats.

1925-11-08.head: Brazilian Diplomat Domício da Gama Dies
1925-11-08.body: Domício da Gama, 62, Brazilian journalist and former Ambassador to Washington, has died.

1925-11-09.head: Rhinelander Divorce Suit Opens
1925-11-09.body: The divorce suit brought by Leonard Kip Rhinelander, heir of a wealthy New York family, against his wife opened at White Plains, New York.

1925-11-10.head: Wu Peifu Defeats Zhang Zuolin Near Xuzhou
1925-11-10.body: Forces of Marshal Wu Peifu have defeated troops of Marshal Zhang Zuolin south of Xuzhou after several days of fighting.
1925-11-10.note: Page places this among events of 9–10 November.

1925-11-10.head: Primate Appoints Committee on Faith Healing
1925-11-10.body: The Archbishop of Canterbury has appointed a committee to examine claims of spiritual healing.

1925-11-11.head: Scientists Begin Unwrapping Tutankhamun's Mummy
1925-11-11.body: Mr Howard Carter and Dr Douglas Derry began the unwrapping and examination of the mummy of King Tutankhamun at Luxor, in the presence of Egyptian officials.

1925-11-11.head: French Fascist League Le Faisceau Founded
1925-11-11.body: Georges Valois has founded Le Faisceau, a French Fascist movement, at a meeting in Paris.

1925-11-12.head: British Submarine M1 Lost in Channel
1925-11-12.body: The British submarine M1 has sunk off Start Point after a collision with a Swedish steamer. Her crew of 69 is believed lost.

1925-11-13.head: Tutankhamun Examination Continues at Luxor
1925-11-13.body: The examination of King Tutankhamun's mummy continued in the Valley of the Kings, with jewels and amulets found among the wrappings.
1925-11-13.note: Ongoing story; the examination ran from 11 to 19 November.

1925-11-14.head: Italy Settles War Debt With America
1925-11-14.body: Italy has agreed terms with the United States for repayment of her war debt at a low rate of interest.

1925-11-14.head: Polish Cabinet of Grabski Resigns
1925-11-14.body: Polish Prime Minister Władysław Grabski and his cabinet have resigned over disagreement about stabilising the zloty.

1925-11-14.head: Australian Nationalists Returned in Election
1925-11-14.body: Mr Bruce's Nationalist government has been returned in the Australian federal election, gaining eleven seats.

1925-11-15.head: Czechoslovakia Holds Parliamentary Elections
1925-11-15.body: Czechoslovakia has held elections to the National Assembly. The Agrarian Party emerged as the largest party.

1925-11-16.head: General Motors Buys Vauxhall Motors
1925-11-16.body: The American General Motors Corporation has purchased the British firm Vauxhall Motors for $2,500,000.

1925-11-17.head: German Mass Murderer Angerstein Executed
1925-11-17.body: Fritz Angerstein, convicted of murdering eight persons, was beheaded at Limburg, Germany.

1925-11-17.head: American Painter Guy Rose Dies
1925-11-17.body: Guy Rose, 58, the American impressionist painter, has died in California.

1925-11-18.head: Commons Approves Locarno Treaties
1925-11-18.body: The House of Commons has approved the Locarno Treaties by 375 votes to 13.

1925-11-18.head: Italian Deputy Rodinò Resigns in Protest
1925-11-18.body: Giulio Rodinò has resigned as Vice-President of the Italian Chamber of Deputies in protest against Fascist authoritarianism.

1925-11-19.head: Tutankhamun Died About Age Eighteen
1925-11-19.body: The examination of Tutankhamun's mummy at Luxor has concluded. The anatomists found the King was about eighteen years of age at death.

1925-11-19.head: Coolidge Urges Entry Into World Court
1925-11-19.body: President Coolidge has called for the United States to join the Permanent Court of International Justice.

1925-11-20.head: Queen Alexandra Dies at Sandringham
1925-11-20.body: Queen Alexandra, the Queen Mother, has died at Sandringham aged 80. She was consort of King Edward VII from 1901 to 1910.

1925-11-20.head: Richthofen Given State Funeral in Berlin
1925-11-20.body: The remains of the airman Manfred von Richthofen were buried in Berlin after a state funeral attended by President Hindenburg.

1925-11-20.head: Skrzyński Forms Polish Government
1925-11-20.body: Count Aleksander Skrzyński, the Foreign Minister, has become Prime Minister of Poland.

1925-11-21.head: German Chemical Firms Agree to Merge
1925-11-21.body: Contracts have been signed merging six leading German chemical companies into a single concern, I.G. Farben.

1925-11-22.head: Painlevé Government Falls in France
1925-11-22.body: The French Cabinet of M. Paul Painlevé has fallen over its financial proposals.

1925-11-22.head: General Guo Songling Revolts Against Zhang Zuolin
1925-11-22.body: General Guo Songling has turned his army against Marshal Zhang Zuolin in Manchuria and is advancing on Mukden.

1925-11-22.head: Chile Elects New Congress
1925-11-22.body: Chile has held elections for the Chamber of Deputies and the Senate.

1925-11-23.head: Manchurian Revolt Spreads
1925-11-23.body: General Guo Songling's forces continued their advance against Marshal Zhang Zuolin's Fengtian army in Manchuria.
1925-11-23.note: Ongoing story; the revolt began on 22 November.

1925-11-24.head: Forrest Theatre Opens on Broadway
1925-11-24.body: The new Forrest Theatre has opened in New York's Broadway district.
1925-11-24.note: Minor item; the month page lists little else for this date.

1925-11-25.head: Turkish Hat Law Comes Into Force
1925-11-25.body: The Turkish law requiring men to wear the Western hat in place of the fez has come into force.

1925-11-26.head: King Vajiravudh of Siam Dies
1925-11-26.body: King Vajiravudh (Rama VI) of Siam has died at Bangkok. His brother, Prince Prajadhipok, succeeds him.

1925-11-26.head: Italy Passes Law on Secret Societies
1925-11-26.body: Italy has promulgated a law bringing secret associations such as the Freemasons under state control.

1925-11-27.head: Queen Alexandra's Funeral at Westminster Abbey
1925-11-27.body: The funeral of Queen Alexandra was held at Westminster Abbey. The Kings of England, Denmark, Norway and Belgium walked in the procession.

1925-11-27.head: Reichstag Approves Locarno Treaties
1925-11-27.body: The German Reichstag has voted to approve the Locarno Treaties.

1925-11-28.head: Briand Forms New French Cabinet
1925-11-28.body: M. Aristide Briand has formed a new French government following the fall of the Painlevé Cabinet.

1925-11-28.head: Queen Alexandra Laid to Rest at Windsor
1925-11-28.body: Queen Alexandra was buried in St George's Chapel, Windsor, beside King Edward VII.

1925-11-28.head: Siam's New King Forms Supreme Council
1925-11-28.body: King Prajadhipok has created a Supreme Council of State of five senior princes to advise the Crown.

1925-11-29.head: Uruguay Holds Parliamentary Elections
1925-11-29.body: Uruguay has held elections for its 123-seat Chamber of Representatives.

1925-11-30.head: Turkey Closes Dervish Lodges
1925-11-30.body: Turkey has ordered the closing of all dervish lodges, tekkes and zawiyas throughout the country.

1925-11-30.head: Australian Seamen's Strike Ends
1925-11-30.body: The Australian seamen's strike has ended after fifteen weeks, with Melbourne the last port to give in.

1925-12-01.head: Locarno Treaties Signed in London
1925-12-01.body: The Locarno Treaties were formally signed at the Foreign Office in London. France also signed mutual guarantee treaties with Poland and Czechoslovakia.

1925-12-01.head: Japan Bans New Farmer-Labour Party
1925-12-01.body: Japan's Farmer-Labour Party was dissolved on government orders within hours of its founding, on grounds of Communist connections.

1925-12-02.head: British Syndicate Wins Bahrain Oil Concession
1925-12-02.body: The Eastern and General Syndicate has signed the first concession to drill for oil in Bahrain.

1925-12-02.head: I.G. Farben Formally Constituted
1925-12-02.body: The merger of six German chemical firms into I.G. Farbenindustrie has been completed.

1925-12-03.head: Irish Boundary Agreement Signed
1925-12-03.body: Representatives of Britain, the Irish Free State and Northern Ireland have signed an agreement leaving the existing Irish border unchanged.

1925-12-03.head: Primo de Rivera Moves Toward Civilian Rule
1925-12-03.body: General Primo de Rivera has replaced Spain's military directory with a civilian cabinet under his presidency.

1925-12-03.head: Romania Sentences Tatarbunary Rebels
1925-12-03.body: A Romanian court-martial has convicted 84 participants in the Tatarbunary rising of 1924.

1925-12-04.head: Italy Gives State Power Over Industry
1925-12-04.body: The Italian Chamber of Deputies has passed a law allowing the government to regulate rates of industrial production.

1925-12-05.head: Medina Surrenders to Ibn Saud
1925-12-05.body: The city of Medina has surrendered to the forces of Sultan Ibn Saud of Nejd without resistance.

1925-12-05.head: Polish Novelist Reymont Dies
1925-12-05.body: Władysław Reymont, 58, the Polish novelist and Nobel prize winner, has died in Warsaw.

1925-12-05.head: Lost Rubens Found in Berlin
1925-12-05.body: A portrait of Saint Teresa of Ávila by Rubens, missing for over 200 years, has been discovered in Berlin.

1925-12-06.head: Egypt Cedes Jaghbub Oasis to Italy
1925-12-06.body: Egypt and Italy have signed an agreement fixing the western frontier, under which the oasis of Jaghbub passes to Italian Libya.

1925-12-06.head: Palestine Jews Elect Representative Assembly
1925-12-06.body: Jews in Palestine voted for an Assembly of Representatives, with 25 lists contesting the election.

1925-12-07.head: Longworth Elected Speaker of House
1925-12-07.body: Mr Nicholas Longworth, Republican, of Ohio, has been elected Speaker of the United States House of Representatives.

1925-12-08.head: New Melkite Patriarch Installed
1925-12-08.body: Cyril IX Moghabghab has been installed as Patriarch of the Melkite Greek Catholic Church.

1925-12-08.head: Coolidge Sends Annual Message to Congress
1925-12-08.body: President Coolidge has transmitted his annual message on the state of the Union to Congress.

1925-12-09.head: Spanish Socialist Leader Pablo Iglesias Dies
1925-12-09.body: Pablo Iglesias, 75, founder of the Spanish Socialist Workers' Party, has died in Madrid.

1925-12-09.head: Governor Wood Vetoes Philippine Plebiscite Bill
1925-12-09.body: General Leonard Wood, Governor-General of the Philippines, has vetoed a bill providing for a plebiscite on independence.

1925-12-10.head: Russian Metropolitan Peter Arrested
1925-12-10.body: Metropolitan Peter of Krutitsy, acting head of the Russian Orthodox Church, has been arrested by the Soviet authorities on conspiracy charges.
1925-12-10.note: Page places this among events of 9–10 December.

1925-12-11.head: Pope Institutes Feast of Christ the King
1925-12-11.body: Pope Pius XI has issued the encyclical 'Quas Primas', establishing the Feast of Christ the King.

1925-12-11.head: Machado Elected President of Portugal
1925-12-11.body: Bernardino Machado has been elected President of the Portuguese Republic.

1925-12-12.head: Reza Khan Proclaimed Shah of Persia
1925-12-12.body: The Persian Constituent Assembly has voted to confer the throne on Reza Khan Pahlavi, founding a new dynasty in place of the Qajars.

1925-12-13.head: Antonio Maura, Spanish Statesman, Dies
1925-12-13.body: Don Antonio Maura, 72, five times Prime Minister of Spain, has died in Madrid.

1925-12-14.head: League Fines Greece Over Bulgarian Incursion
1925-12-14.body: The League of Nations Council has settled the Greek-Bulgarian dispute and ordered Greece to pay an indemnity to Bulgaria for the Petrich incursion.

1925-12-14.head: Berg's Opera 'Wozzeck' Premiered in Berlin
1925-12-14.body: Alban Berg's opera 'Wozzeck' had its first performance at the Berlin State Opera.

1925-12-15.head: Reza Shah Takes Oath in Teheran
1925-12-15.body: Reza Khan took the oath before the Persian Constituent Assembly as Shah, the first of the Pahlavi dynasty.

1925-12-15.head: Boxer Battling Siki Killed in New York
1925-12-15.body: Battling Siki, the Senegalese former light-heavyweight champion of the world, has been found shot dead in New York.

1925-12-16.head: League Awards Mosul to Iraq
1925-12-16.body: The League of Nations Council has decided that the Mosul vilayet shall belong to Iraq, under British mandate, despite Turkish objections.

1925-12-16.head: Broadcasting Begins in Ceylon
1925-12-16.body: Colombo Radio has begun transmitting, introducing wireless broadcasting to Ceylon.

1925-12-17.head: Turkey and Russia Sign Neutrality Pact
1925-12-17.body: Turkey and the Soviet Union have signed a treaty of friendship and neutrality in Paris, the day after the Mosul award to Iraq.

1925-12-17.head: Colonel Mitchell Found Guilty
1925-12-17.body: Colonel William Mitchell has been convicted by court-martial on all charges of insubordination.

1925-12-18.head: Soviet Communist Party Congress Opens
1925-12-18.body: The 14th Congress of the Communist Party of the Soviet Union has opened in Moscow with 1,306 delegates.

1925-12-18.head: Silva Again Portuguese Prime Minister
1925-12-18.body: António Maria da Silva has become Prime Minister of Portugal for the fourth time.

1925-12-18.head: Sculptor Sir Hamo Thornycroft Dies
1925-12-18.body: Sir Hamo Thornycroft, 75, the British sculptor, has died.

1925-12-19.head: Jeddah Surrenders; King Ali Abdicates
1925-12-19.body: Jeddah has surrendered to Sultan Ibn Saud after a siege of ten months. King Ali of the Hejaz has abdicated and is leaving the country.

1925-12-20.head: Chilean Philanthropist Santa María Dies
1925-12-20.body: Federico Santa María, the Chilean benefactor who left his fortune for a technical university at Valparaíso, has died in Paris.
1925-12-20.note: Quiet day on the month page; minor item.

1925-12-21.head: Former French Premier Méline Dies
1925-12-21.body: M. Jules Méline, 87, former Prime Minister of France and author of the protective tariff of 1892, has died.

1925-12-21.head: 'Battleship Potemkin' Shown at Bolshoi
1925-12-21.body: Sergei Eisenstein's film 'Battleship Potemkin' received a special showing at the Bolshoi Theatre, Moscow.

1925-12-22.head: Princess Dowager Alice of Monaco Dies
1925-12-22.body: Alice, Princess Dowager of Monaco, has died in Paris.

1925-12-22.head: Publisher Frank Munsey Dies
1925-12-22.body: Frank A. Munsey, 71, the American newspaper and magazine proprietor, has died in New York.

1925-12-23.head: Jouvenel High Commissioner of the Levant
1925-12-23.body: M. Henry de Jouvenel has been installed as French High Commissioner in Syria and the Lebanon.
1925-12-23.note: Month page lists his appointment among events of 23 December.

1925-12-23.head: Figueroa Inaugurated President of Chile
1925-12-23.body: Emiliano Figueroa has been inaugurated as President of Chile.

1925-12-24.head: Mussolini's Powers Enlarged by Law
1925-12-24.body: The Italian Parliament has passed a law making the head of government responsible to the King alone and placing his powers beyond parliamentary review.

1925-12-24.head: Rebel General Guo Songling Executed
1925-12-24.body: General Guo Songling, whose revolt against Marshal Zhang Zuolin has collapsed, was captured and executed in Manchuria.

1925-12-24.head: Pope Closes Holy Door; Jubilee Ends
1925-12-24.body: Pope Pius XI closed the Holy Door at St Peter's, ending the Holy Year.

1925-12-25.head: Syrian Rebel Leader al-Kharrat Killed
1925-12-25.body: Hasan al-Kharrat, a leader of the insurgents in the Ghouta around Damascus, was killed in fighting with French forces.

1925-12-25.head: Psychoanalyst Karl Abraham Dies
1925-12-25.body: Dr Karl Abraham, 48, the Berlin psychoanalyst, has died.

1925-12-26.head: Turkey Adopts the European Calendar
1925-12-26.body: The Turkish Grand National Assembly has passed a law requiring the Gregorian calendar for all government affairs.

1925-12-26.head: Communist Party Organised in India
1925-12-26.body: A Communist Party of India was formally organised at a conference in Cawnpore.

1925-12-26.head: Italy Ends Revolt in Somaliland
1925-12-26.body: Italian forces have recaptured El Buur and put an end to the rebellion in the Sultanate of Obbia in Italian Somaliland.

1925-12-27.head: Coptic Archbishop of Jerusalem Consecrated
1925-12-27.body: Basil III has become Coptic Archbishop of Jerusalem, Palestine and the Near East.

1925-12-27.head: Mexican Mine Explosion Kills 52
1925-12-27.body: An explosion in a coal mine near Palaú, Coahuila, Mexico, has killed 52 miners.

1925-12-28.head: Crown Prince Carol Renounces Romanian Throne
1925-12-28.body: Crown Prince Carol of Romania has renounced his right of succession. His young son Michael becomes heir to the throne.

1925-12-28.head: Poet Sergei Yesenin Dies in Leningrad
1925-12-28.body: Sergei Yesenin, 30, the Russian poet, has been found dead in a Leningrad hotel.

1925-12-29.head: Floods Sweep Central Europe
1925-12-29.body: Severe floods have struck Europe. Hungary and Romania are the worst hit, with about 100 persons reported dead.

1925-12-29.head: Swiss Painter Félix Vallotton Dies
1925-12-29.body: Félix Vallotton, 60, the Swiss-born painter and engraver, has died in Paris.

1925-12-30.head: 'Ben-Hur' Film Opens in New York
1925-12-30.body: The film 'Ben-Hur' has had its American premiere at the George M. Cohan Theatre, New York.

1925-12-31.head: Italy Empowers Government to Close Newspapers
1925-12-31.body: The Italian Parliament has approved a press law allowing the government to suppress opposition newspapers.

1925-12-31.head: Belgium Suffers Worst Floods Since 1876
1925-12-31.body: Belgium is suffering its worst floods since 1876.
